findings.title: Fetch the archived baseline before running the new compatibility gate
findings.description: The added required CI command invokes scripts/native-game-migration-compat.mjs, whose line 30 unconditionally archives commit 5386a8cd3cf3e4360fd55f8f06bc84d159ff540b. The checkout at lines 19-21 leaves actions/checkout's default fetch-depth of 1, and no subsequent step fetches that baseline. A fresh checkout of the reviewed source therefore lacks the required Git object: the compatibility script fails at stage archive and exits 1, making linux-foundation fail even though the PostgreSQL scenarios pass when both commits are present. This prevents the advertised exact-source Ubuntu verification from being reproducible.

The archive exits 128: fatal: not a tree object: 5386a8cd3cf3e4360fd55f8f06bc84d159ff540b.

After checking out a1bd5b116125a1d2675568ae0c5a02cc4d62d9dc inside that clone and linking installed external dependencies, run node scripts/with-test-db.mjs node --import tsx scripts/native-game-migration-compat.mjs. The unchanged script exits 1 at archive; its recorded git archive exits 128. Its owned test database and network are cleaned up.

Retain the actual historical-source archive/build and exact-prefix checksum policy. Verify the corrected workflow from a fresh checkout and obtain successful exact-source Ubuntu evidence before coordinator acceptance.

assessment: The two stated VL-016 acceptance scenarios pass locally with the necessary Git history: actual PG concurrency admits one settlement and the actual archived47 runtime passes declared exact-prefix expansion/rollback. CI reproducibility remains blocked by VL016-R1.

The parent-row lock plus insert triggers reject stale receipt/settlement epoch or version; unique match/version and actor/command keys protect distinct transition and replay collisions. Events and outbox reference real matching parent records. Atomicity is demonstrated for caller-owned SQL transactions, not supplied by independent statements or a Rust command host.

Cascade probes remove child receipt/event/settlement/outbox data within the native graph without platform foreign keys. They do not establish account deletion/export, security retention or reliable delivery of pending effects across deletion; those remain explicit future owner/consumer contracts before activation.

Private snapshots, receipts and canonical events have bounded envelope columns. Actual AEAD fixture roundtrip survives old-runtime rollback. SQL cannot prove encryption, associated-data binding, fresh nonce/key handling, or prevent low-entropy metadata disclosure; no public projection or native route is added here.

Catalog probes confirm a table namespace in the existing search path, default table ACLs, no RLS and invoker-rights trigger functions. This migration grants no platform rights and is not a provisioned schema/role isolation boundary. Restricting runtime DML, using a different migration identity and defining deletion/retention privileges remain required before a real host is activated.

Checkpoint identity and monotonic clocks are guarded, but exact +1 transitions, immutable receipt/settlement DML policy, authenticated owner acquisition, expected lifecycle CAS, participant/session/policy authorization and economy inbox effects remain host responsibilities as documented. This review does not broaden the task into full Rust runtime authentication.
limitations: Verification was local Linux with existing pinned installed dependencies. No hosted Ubuntu run or fresh network dependency install was initiated. Full workspace lint/typecheck/governance/OCI/Rust suites were not independently rerun; focused TypeScript builds, PG tests, compatibility, workflow governance and preservation are the actual scopes recorded above.

No Unity, Windows, physical-GPU, production schema/backup/rollback, public deployment, native admission, real Rust host, economy consumer or complete privacy/retention qualification is claimed. Runtime remains default-off and the legacy Nest RoomAuthority remains sole legacy writer.

All authored files are this new review and ignored artifacts under artifacts/desktop-first/vl016/. No source, handoff, scheduler state, reservation, checksum baseline, checkpoint document or commit was edited. The existing modified live-state and untracked handoff were left as found. .idea and infra/botkeep-ca.pem were not read or staged. No agent was spawned.

Reviewer setup/probe failures and their corrected successful runs are retained rather than treated as application defects. VL016-R1 is independently reproduced both with direct Git and the unchanged wrapper-driven compatibility script in a genuine shallow clone.
